excerpt: Ask for the cut. The agent reads your footage, makes the edit, and leaves every clip on the timeline for you to move.
Every clip is transcribed, described shot by shot, and knows who’s in it.
Save a filter and it becomes a smart bin that fills as footage arrives.
Cut camera originals with no transcode. RED, Blackmagic RAW, ProRes, DNxHR and MXF play as the camera or Avid wrote them.
Send a link. Comments land on your timeline, and the agent can answer them.
Connect Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT or Cursor to Kino’s MCP server, and they can search your footage and edit your projects.
Cloud agents like Dot, Muse, Grok Bot and Devin install Kino on their own computer and edit while you’re away.
Copy originals into Kino for clipping while you keep editing in Premiere or another editor.
Queue a copy of one file from an HTTPS URL into the bin assigned to your organization API key.
Your agent is great at motion graphics and animation in Kino.
Start with craft. 100+ templates: titles, maps, captions and transitions.
Manage many variants of your video and ask the agent to one-shot each.
Share any clip as a link, and search by what’s on screen.
Conversion runs on the user's device without an account.
Every clip streams from Kino, so a project opens the same on any machine.
A user tried Kino head to head with Claude Code directly to make a simple video. They found Kino 'way easier to nudge and control' and said it 'just works', which they called rare in software.

A user is 'really enjoying kino.ai' and finds it 'a bit more user friendly than hyperframes'. They found Claude 'a bit worse' inside it, but said it is still very usable and the issue might be their own prompting.

A user uses Claude to make short explainer videos for themselves and teammates. Their reading is that Kino works best when you already have footage, not when starting from scratch, so it may not suit that use case.

A former podcast producer praised the product but didn't see templates. They want reusable formats (title design, intro music, trailer clips, social cuts) so the agent could produce a full episode with a few commands. They called a template builder guided by the agent the 'holy grail'.

On Kino Transcode, Kino's browser tool for opening RED and Blackmagic RAW files, a user said it's 'pretty snappy'. They noted it's annoying to find legitimate file conversion tools online and said they'll check out the Kino editor.
